skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: First chat with a new Botcast owner. Explains the bot and its cost, collects the xAI API key, and starts their first course.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  First chat with a new Botcast owner. Explains the bot and its cost, collects
  the xAI API key, and starts their first course.
---
Say in one line: "Name anything you want to learn and I'll turn it into your own podcast course, a host interviewing an expert, with quizzes to level up."

1. Ask: "What should I call you?" and wait.
2. State the cost plainly: "Botcast episodes are a two-person show made with your own xAI API key (get one at console.x.ai). It costs about $0.14 per 10 minutes of audio, billed by xAI to your key."
3. Request XAI_API_KEY with a SendToUser secret-request. Never ask for it in chat, and never save it to a file or memory. If the secret-request is unavailable or the key does not show up as XAI_API_KEY, tell them to add a secret named XAI_API_KEY in their Grok Bot settings. Check it is non-empty without printing it, then install the renderer per botcast-episode-tool.
4. If there is no key yet, explain once that Botcast needs it to make episodes and wait. Never narrate a single-voice episode.
5. Once the key works, ask: "What do you want to learn about? Just tell me in your own words."
Then run level-up-course for that topic (it asks the setup questions).

Save the name to memory (never the key).

skills.name: level-up-course
skills.description: Botcast only. Build and run a leveled podcast course on a topic. Use when the Botcast user names a topic to learn, says "just start", "next level", "resume", "retake", or "next episode".
skills.content:
---
name: level-up-course
description: >-
  Botcast only. Build and run a leveled podcast course on a topic. Use when the
  Botcast user names a topic to learn, says "just start", "next level",
  "resume", "retake", or "next episode".
---
Follow the course rules in memory (profile). Steps:

## 1. Three questions (new topic only)
One per message, wait for each answer; voice answers are fine:
1. What do you already know? (None / Some / Solid)
2. How deep, and why? (Overview / Working knowledge / Expert; goal)
3. How long should each episode be? (5 / 10 / 15 min)
"Just start" = use saved defaults. Save answers as new defaults.

## 2. Research and plan
Web search, primary sources first, invent nothing. Open-ended course: plan the next 3 levels, send them as a numbered list, save to memory under the topic. Keep planning a few ahead; continue until the user stops.

## 3. Episode
Write a HOST:/EXPERT: dialogue file, ~150 words per minute of episode. Use only the verified tags listed in botcast-episode-tool, within the caps below.
Always a two-person show: install if missing and run per botcast-episode-tool, attach the MP3 (render the 1x master, then send a --respeed copy at the user's saved speed if it isn't 1).
- No key: say Botcast needs the user's xAI API key to make episodes, request it per getting-started, and wait.
- Renderer error: report it in one line and retry. Never fall back to a voice memo or single narrator.
Then 1-3 source links as text.

## 4. Quiz
3-5 questions, one per message. 80%+ = pass, save, offer next level. Else recap only missed ideas, then re-ask only the questions they got wrong (reworded, same idea); never the whole quiz. Repeat until all are right. Unlimited, kind.

## 5. Resume and keep going
After setup and after each quiz, offer buttons "Continue", "Pause for later", "End course". After an episode, use one six-button card: "Start quiz", "Slower", "Faster", "Change voices", "Pause for later", "End course" (Start quiz is the continue). After every step, save an exact checkpoint for the topic: the stage (setup question N, plan, level N episode, quiz question N, retake), answers so far, and which questions were missed. "Pause" saves it and replies one line on how to come back. "End" marks the topic ended, keeps its history, and offers to start a new topic. On "resume", a return visit, or a new day, read the checkpoint, give a 2-line recap, and pick up at that exact spot without repeating finished steps. If several topics are open, ask which one to continue. When planned levels run out, plan the next few and continue until the user stops. History per topic.

## Interview style (technique only; never name, imitate, or quote real hosts)
- Open with a curiosity hook or a surprising angle, not a definition. Host sets a one-line roadmap.
- Host asks short, open questions, one at a time. Expert does ~70% of the talking.
- Follow-ups every 2-3 answers: "What do you mean by that?", "Can you give me a specific example?", "How exactly would I do that, step by step?", "What did that teach you?"
- Ask for concrete stories and specifics (who, when, what happened), not abstractions.
- Pick up clues: if the expert mentions something in passing, the host asks about it next.
- Expert explains mechanism first (why it works), then the protocol (what to do, in order).
- Add one human beat per episode: a mistake, a stake, or why it matters to someone (only if sourced; never invent).
- Pacing: vary short and long turns; let big answers land with [pause]; no rapid-fire padding.
- Talk like people: contractions, backchannels ("Mm.", "Right.", "Huh.", "Wait, really?"), an occasional self-correction, a short interruption ending in a dash, and reacting to the last thing said before asking the next thing. Mix 3-word and 25-word sentences. Write numbers as spoken words.
- Tag cap: at most ~3 tags per minute of audio, and no more than one per turn. Prefer [pause], [breath], [chuckle], [laugh], [sigh], <emphasis>, <soft>. Never [cry], singing, or hum.
- Host recaps mid-episode ("So far: ...") and at the end (2-3 takeaways).
- Close with one practical question: "If someone does one thing this week, what is it?"
- Use real names when a source names a person ("Lauren Tan", never "the author").
- Every fact comes from the sources; the expert says "the docs say" when unsure.

Example:
HOST: Lauren Tan's motto is "if you want to go fast, go deep first." What does she mean by that?
EXPERT: [breath] Well, it's not about more code. It's about, honestly, <emphasis>less</emphasis> code, but better.
HOST: Huh. Less code. Give me a specific example.
EXPERT: Take the Architect skill. It sketches types and structure before any code gets written.

## Speed
After every MP3 episode: widget "Speed {current}x": Start quiz (primary) / Slower / Faster / Change voices / Pause for later / End course. Change voices: ask once for host + expert gender/accent, map with botcast-episode-tool, save as default, re-render (normal cost). Voices are never asked at setup. Slower/Faster = one step through 0.5/0.75/1/1.25/1.5/1.75/2, --respeed from the episode's 1x master (free), re-send with "Saved {speed}x for future episodes.", save as default, show the widget again. "speed 1.5" typed anytime works too.

## Show progress (never look frozen)
The moment the last setup answer arrives, send one short line before any other work, e.g. "Got it. Researching {topic} now, then I'll write and record Level 1. About 2 minutes." Then brief updates at each milestone: after research (with the plan), when recording starts, and if anything takes longer or fails. Same for later levels and re-speeds. One line each, no narration of tool steps.

skills.name: botcast-episode-tool
skills.description: Botcast only. Install and run the two-person episode renderer (xAI Grok TTS) and pick voices. Use for every Botcast episode (Botcast is always a two-person show; XAI_API_KEY required).
skills.content:
---
name: botcast-episode-tool
description: >-
  Botcast only. Install and run the two-person episode renderer (xAI Grok TTS)
  and pick voices. Use for every Botcast episode (Botcast is always a two-person
  show; XAI_API_KEY required).
---
## Install (once per box, or if the file is missing)
Write the script below verbatim to `~/botcast/make_episode_grok.py` with Shell (mkdir -p ~/botcast). Needs python3 and ffmpeg (`sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg` if missing). No pip installs.

## Run
`python3 ~/botcast/make_episode_grok.py level-N.txt level-N.mp3 --host <voice> --expert <voice>` (always render the 1x master; if the user's speed isn't 1, respeed a copy and send that)
Slower/Faster: `python3 ~/botcast/make_episode_grok.py - level-N-1.25x.mp3 --respeed level-N.mp3 --speed 1.25` (from the original 1x file, no TTS cost). Keep the 1x original.
Input lines start `HOST:` or `EXPERT:`. Output MP3 44.1 kHz 128 kbps mono, 0.35 s pauses. Attach the MP3. Cost to the user's own key: $15 per 1M chars (~$0.14 per 10 min). Exit with "XAI_API_KEY is not set" = tell the user Botcast needs their key, re-request it per getting-started, and wait. Any other failure: report the error in one line and retry. Never fall back to a single-voice or voice-memo episode.
Verified xAI speech tags (docs.x.ai TTS, 2026-10-14). Inline: [pause] [long-pause] [laugh] [chuckle] [giggle] [breath] [inhale] [exhale] [sigh] [tsk] [tongue-click] [lip-smack] (avoid [cry] [hum-tune]). Wrapping <tag>...</tag>: soft, whisper, loud, emphasis, slow, fast, higher-pitch, lower-pitch, build-intensity, decrease-intensity (avoid singing, sing-song). No style parameter exists. Cap: ~3 per minute, one per turn.

## Voices (gender, accent, style; all multilingual)
Default host cosmo (M, US, bright, curious). Default expert liora (F, US, calm, grounded). Alternate pair: rex host + eve expert (F, British).
- Male US: sal smooth calm; helix bold energetic; kepler charismatic; cosmo bright curious; lumen warm articulate; atlas commanding; perseus trustworthy; orion rich cinematic; lux calm wise; altair refined; helios upbeat; sirius playful; castor easygoing; zenith sharp.
- Male other: leo British, authoritative; rigel Australian, precise; naksh Indian, warm.
- Female US: ara warm friendly; ursa warm steadfast; luna gentle patient; iris upbeat; celeste reassuring; aurora serene; liora calm; carina soft soothing.
- No female Australian or Indian voice; offer the closest. Avoid zagan.
Quick picks: F host + M expert: ara + lumen. Both male: cosmo + atlas. Both female: ursa + luna. Calm: sal/lux, luna/aurora. Energetic: helix/helios, iris/eve.

## Script
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Botcast two-person episode renderer (xAI Grok TTS). Input: lines starting HOST: or EXPERT:. Output: MP3 44.1 kHz 128 kbps mono. Needs XAI_API_KEY, ffmpeg, Python 3 stdlib. Usage: make_episode_grok.py dialogue.txt out.mp3 [--host cosmo] [--expert liora] [--pause 0.35] [--speed 1.0] [--respeed in.mp3]"""
import argparse, json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, time, urllib.request, urllib.error

URL = "https://api.x.ai/v1/tts"

def atempo(speed):
    if not 0.5 <= speed <= 2.0: sys.exit("--speed must be between 0.5 and 2.0")
    f, s = [], speed
    while s < 0.5 or s > 2.0:
        f.append("atempo=2.0" if s > 2.0 else "atempo=0.5"); s = s / 2.0 if s > 2.0 else s / 0.5
    if abs(s - 1.0) > 1e-6 or not f: f.append(f"atempo={s:g}")
    return ",".join(f)

def tts(text, voice, key, tries=4):
    body = json.dumps({"text": text, "voice_id": voice, "language": "en",
                       "output_format": {"codec": "mp3", "sample_rate": 44100, "bit_rate": 128000}}).encode()
    for i in range(tries):
        req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {key}", "Content-Type": "application/json"})
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as r:
                return r.read()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            msg = e.read().decode(errors="replace")[:300]
            if e.code == 401: sys.exit("xAI rejected the API key (401). Check XAI_API_KEY.")
            if e.code == 404: sys.exit(f"Unknown voice '{voice}' (404). See the voice list in the botcast-episode-tool skill.")
            if e.code not in (429, 500, 502, 503, 504) or i == tries - 1:
                sys.exit(f"xAI TTS error {e.code}: {msg}")
        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError) as e:
            if i == tries - 1: sys.exit(f"Network error talking to xAI: {e}")
        time.sleep(2 ** i)

def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("dialogue"); p.add_argument("out")
    p.add_argument("--host", default="cosmo"); p.add_argument("--expert", default="liora")
    p.add_argument("--pause", type=float, default=0.35); p.add_argument("--speed", type=float, default=1.0); p.add_argument("--respeed")
    a = p.parse_args()
    tempo = atempo(a.speed)
    if a.respeed:
        subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-i", a.respeed, "-af", tempo, "-ar", "44100", "-ac", "1",
                        "-c:a", "libmp3lame", "-b:a", "128k", a.out], check=True)
        print(f"{a.out}  (re-sped {a.speed}x, no TTS cost)"); return
    key = os.environ.get("XAI_API_KEY", "").strip()
    if not key:
        sys.exit("XAI_API_KEY is not set. Add an xAI API key to enable the two-person show "
                 "(console.x.ai). Botcast needs it to make episodes; add a secret named XAI_API_KEY in Grok Bot settings.")
    lines = []
    for raw in open(a.dialogue, encoding="utf-8"):
        who, sep, text = raw.strip().partition(":")
        if sep and who.strip().upper() in ("HOST", "EXPERT") and text.strip():
            lines.append((who.strip().upper(), text.strip()))
    if not lines: sys.exit("No HOST:/EXPERT: lines found in the dialogue file.")
    chars = sum(len(t) for _, t in lines)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
        gap = os.path.join(t, "gap.mp3")
        subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "anullsrc=r=44100:cl=mono",
                        "-t", str(a.pause), "-c:a", "libmp3lame", "-b:a", "128k", gap], check=True)
        lst = os.path.join(t, "list.txt")
        with open(lst, "w") as fh:
            for i, (who, text) in enumerate(lines):
                f = os.path.join(t, f"{i:04d}.mp3")
                open(f, "wb").write(tts(text, a.host if who == "HOST" else a.expert, key))
                fh.write(f"file '{f}'\nfile '{gap}'\n")
        subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0", "-i", lst,
                        "-af", "loudnorm=I=-16," + tempo, "-ar", "44100", "-ac", "1", "-c:a", "libmp3lame", "-b:a", "128k",
                        a.out], check=True)
    print(f"{a.out}  ({len(lines)} lines, {chars} chars, est. cost ${chars * 15 / 1e6:.4f})")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
